title: Processing Picking Management Work

children:
Picking Management is a different way to view and execute the work within 
 the warehouse. Through regular work execution, each work unit must be 
 completed by one user, moving throughout the warehouse and completing 
 all the work for that work unit. Picking management provides a way for 
 work to broken up by zone, and executed by multiple users. The procedures 
 in this topic describe how to execute work in the various screens of the 
 Picking Management module. Note that in order for a work unit to appear in the Picking Management Explorer/Picking Window, the  Pick 
 Management Active check box must be selected on the work unit's associated work zone and work type configuration records.
Identifying a Quality Measures Reason Code

Assigning/Unassigning an Instruction 
 to a Team/User

- This window appears when you select multiple zones in the Picking Management 
 Explorer, and choose the View Summary right-click option.
- This window appears when you right-click a work unit record (in the Picking Selection Window) and choose Open.
The following is discussed in this topic:

Signing/Scanning on to a 
 Picking Terminal (on 
 the Picking Signon Window)

Assigning a Work Unit (on the 
 Start Picking Window)
Starting a Pick (on the Start Picking Window)
Completing a Pick (on the Complete Picking Window)
1. Signing/Scanning on to a Picking Terminal (on the Picking Signon Window)...

To initiate work, you need to first sign or scan on to the appropriate 
 picking terminal. Once you are logged on, you can select a zone from the 
 appropriate picking terminal. You can perform this action on the Picking 
 Signon Window. This window will display all of the zone(s) that are active 
 for picking management.

Choose the Picking Signon option 
 from the desktop. The system will display the Picking Signon 
 Window.

Right-click a work unit record 
 in the Picking Management Explorer and choose the Scan On option. 
 The system will display the Picking Signon Window.

Select the work 
 zone that you want to pick from and press OK. The system will display 
 the Picking Selection Window. If you signed on using the "scan on" 
 option, the work unit you selected will populate the Work Unit field of 
 the Picking Selection Window.
2. Assigning a Work Unit (on the Start Picking Window)...

Before a pick can be executed, you need to assign a work unit to a user. 
 The system will display all of the work units (open, on hold, and assigned) 
 in your selected zone in the Picking Selection Window. This window sorts 
 the units in order by zones away, which indicates which zone is currently 
 ready to be picked into the shipping container. You can also see the first 
 and last location that you must pick from, as well as the total quantity 
 you must pick. Note that a user can be assigned to multiple work units.

Each work unit is represented by 
 a graphical icon. This icon indicates the status of each unit. Below are 
 explanations of what each icon represents:

Represents a work unit that has a user 
 assigned to it.
Represents a work unit that has been placed on hold.

Access the Picking Selection Window. 
 The system displays this window after you choose a zone to work in from 
 the Picking Signon Window.

If necessary, research work unit(s) 
 by selecting a work unit from the record list and pressing the 
 Details Button. The system will display the Picking Details Window. Press 
 OK when finished.

Select the work unit that 
 has a zones away value of 0. This represents the zone that you should 
 pick from.

Enter the user name that 
 you want to assign to the work unit.

Enter the work unit number 
 you want to assign in the Work Unit Field.

If needed, press the Print Button 
 if you want to print a work pick list for this work unit.

Press OK. 
 The system will assign the work unit.

3. Starting a Pick (on 
 the Start Picking Window)...

Once a user has been assigned to a work unit, you will need to confirm 
 the that the pick information is correct. You can perform this action 
 in the Start Picking Window. If appropriate, you can unassign a user as 
 the picker associated with this work unit. You can also view zone details 
 from this window.

Press the Details Button 
 to view individual work instruction information from the Picking Details 
 Window.

If necessary, you can unassign 
 this work unit by pressing the Unassign Button. The system will 
 unassign the work unit from the current user and display the Picking Selection 
 Window.

To start picking, press OK. 
 The system will display the Picking Selection Window.

Enter your user 
 name and the work unit you want to pick and press OK. The system 
 will display the Complete Picking Window.

4. Completing a Pick (on 
 the Complete Picking Window)...

You can execute a picking action on the Complete Picking Window. This 
 window will appear when you enter a work unit on the Picking Selection 
 Window that has been previously assigned to you.

Access the Complete Picking Window 
 from the Picking Selection Window.

To Pick: Press OK; the system will perform the pick action, 
 and close the work unit.

To Hold: Press the Hold Button; the system will display the 
 Work Hold Window. Enter the hold code that you want to apply to the instruction. 
 The value you enter as a hold code will depend on your business practices. 
 The system will display this code on the Work Instruction Window. Press 
 OK. The system will place this instruction on hold. You can release this 
 work unit from the Work Insight Screen. Note that if an instruction is on hold, 
 you cannot perform any actions on it until it is released. Also, the current 
 instruction(s) will not be confirmed.

To Short Pick: Press the Short Pick Button; the system will 
 display the Picking Short Pick Window. Enter the item and quantity data 
 of the item you want to short pick. If the item is lot controlled, you 
 will need to enter the lot ID as well. Press OK. The system will display 
 the Complete Picking Window. Press OK again. The system will display the 
 Quality Measures Window. Enter a reason code for your short pick and press 
 OK. The system will perform the short pick and display the Picking Selection 
 Window.

You can unassign a user from an open work unit. This is helpful if for 
 some reason the assigned user cannot perform a pick. A user cannot be 
 unassigned from a work unit if that unit is on hold. You can also unassign 
 a work unit from the Picking Management Explorer.

Access the Start Picking Window 
 or the Complete Picking Window.

Select the work 
 unit that you want to unassign and press the Unassign Button. The 
 system will remove the user associated with the unit, and return you to 
 the Picking Selection Window.
